text.p: Mayne Nickless Ltd said on Tuesday it sees its healthcare operations as a key driver to growth in the next two-to-four years, along with its time critical express and contract logistics business.

"There will continue to be a strong emphasis on health care, and support for its further development through significant strategic investment both here and overseas," outgoing chairman Ian Webber told the annual meeting.
"We expect it (healthcare) to be a key driver of growth in the next two-to-four years," Webber said.

Webber said healthcare diversification would be focussed on the services it offers in Australia and offshore, particularly in Asia. "Our position in health care makes us ideally suited to export our expertise."
He said Mayne had just acquired private New South Wales pathology provider Hampson Pathology for an undisclosed sum.
The focus on health care did not mean that its core businesses would be neglected, he said.
"We intend to grow in contract logistics and time critical express through careful investment and complementary acquistions," Webber said.
"The company does not believe that acquisitions are the only, or even preferred method for growth. The board will only consider this path when an addition has a precise strategic fit," Webber said.

"We are seeking a portfolio that has the right mix of mature businesses, which can generate strong return, growing businesses, and developmental businesses which we can build on into the future,"" he said.
He said healthcare and contract logistics fit the growth category. "A longer term aim is to have 15 percent of our assets in Asia in the next 10 years," he said.
Webber also announced he planned to retire and that director Mark Raynor would succeed him as chairman in 1997.
At 11.55 a.m. (0055 GMT), Mayne shares were five cents lower at A$8.32.
